samples.question: A single straight black line crosses this picture; treat that line as a mirror. On one side of the line there are five coloured disks: one red, one blue, one green, one orange and one purple. On the other side of the line there are five gray squares, all exactly the same size and the same shade, so the squares carry no colour information at all. The mirror image of a point is the point at the same perpendicular distance from the line, on the other side, along the perpendicular through it. Exactly four of the five gray squares are centred precisely on the mirror image of the centre of one of the disks, and each of those four squares belongs to a different disk. The remaining gray square is displaced: it is not centred on the mirror image of any disk. So exactly one disk has no gray square at its mirror image. What is the colour of that one disk? Answer red, blue, green, orange, or purple.
